title: Add a title: search-and-pick
spec: The primary success criterion. A search field; typing shows candidate cards WITH POSTERS as you type (debounced); clicking one adds it — title, year, kind, summary, artwork, IMDb link and genres all populated from T-3 with zero typing. Optional 'why' field, free text, one line. New titles append to the end of the queue with status=queued. Duplicate tmdb_id is refused with a clear message pointing at the existing entry. HARD RULE: no field for summary, poster URL, or IMDb link is ever presented to the user — if a human is typing metadata this ticket has failed. ACCEPT: adding Cowboy Bebop takes one search and one click, and the resulting record carries poster, backdrop, summary, year, kind and a working IMDb link.

locate.evidence: LOCATE at .autodev/locates/T-4.md: T-4 adds no source-integration code — /api/search, /api/details and cache() from T-3 are the whole capture path, and every column it writes already exists from T-2. Four constraints found by reading that code: IntegrityError on the (source,source_id) unique index is the race-safe duplicate signal so a SELECT-first check would be wrong; db.execute opens a connection per call; detail is a TEXT/JSON column so media_type must be merged in rather than given a new column; and no client router exists yet, so T-4 introduces the minimum one instead of leaving T-5 and T-6 to each invent their own. Also records that the add view must use base.css's existing component classes and declare no colours, or alternate skins stop covering it.

plan.evidence: PLAN at .autodev/plans/T-4.md, 6 steps mapped to ACs. Two decisions recorded: a 250ms debounce that also ABORTS the in-flight request when a newer keystroke lands, because without the abort results arrive out of order and the grid answers a query the user has already typed past; and delete deliberately not evicting cached artwork, since files are content-addressed and two titles can share an image — recorded so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight. Step 4 introduces the minimal client router T-5 and T-6 will both need, rather than leaving each to invent one.

AC2 proven by DOM AUDIT — the entire add flow contains exactly two inputs, the search box and why; no field exists for summary, poster URL, link or genre. AC3: stored rows carry detail.media_type (tv for Cowboy Bebop, movie for The Thing), discharging T-3's recorded obligation. AC4: re-adding Cowboy Bebop returned 409 naming the existing entry and the table still held one row. AC5: positions 10/20/30, gap-tolerant per T-7. AC7: zero stored rows hold a remote URL. AC9: remove took the grid from 3 cards to 2. One defect found and fixed mid-ticket: the brand button kept its native border and rendered as a box; reset in base.css, re-verified borderTopWidth 0px. Final run: zero pageerrors and zero console errors. Gaps: games unproven (IGDB credentials incomplete), Chromium only.

auto-review.evidence: REVIEWED. No new defects survived: the one found during the build (brand button border) was fixed and re-verified before this stage. Deliberate decisions re-examined and left standing, each with its reason: (1) duplicates are caught via sqlite3.IntegrityError on the (source,source_id) unique index rather than a SELECT-then-INSERT, which is the only race-safe option; (2) DELETE does not evict cached artwork because files are content-addressed and two titles can legitimately share an image, so reference counting would cost more than the bytes; (3) the search debounce also ABORTS the in-flight request, without which a slow early response can land after a fast later one and the grid answers a query the user has typed past — this is why AC6 measures requests rather than trusting the timer; (4) the outbound link is DERIVED at serialisation from imdb_id or detail.igdb_url rather than stored, because a single stored link column would be null for every game. All new component classes (.grid, .card__frame, .card__remove, .card__why, .addbar, .hint, .nav) were added to base.css rather than to a view, so alternate skins keep covering surfaces written after them — verified by screenshotting the populated list under nocturne.
